assessments.rationale: The forecasted six differs from the stipulated outcome of four.
assessments.scope: Numeric outcome at the stipulated T2 horizon only.

authorStipulatedConditions.statement: The forecast declares assumptions at T1 and the fixture stipulates four arrivals at T2.

claims.proposition: Six synthetic arrivals will occur by T2 under assumptions A and B.
claims.scope: The declared fixture process and assumptions.
claims.temporalQualifier: Forecast at T1 for horizon T2.

cases.declaredQuestion: Does a missed outcome imply the forecast was irrational or deceptive?

evidence.description: The stipulated T2 outcome contains four arrivals.

expressions.form: Under assumptions A and B, six arrivals are predicted by T2.
expressions.interpretationNote: The assumptions and T2 horizon are explicit.

cases.lesson: Ex-ante warrant and later outcome are different assessment targets.
nonClaims: A failed prediction is not a liar classification.
Forecast quality is not aggregated into a score.

assessments.limitations: The unperformed alternative is not treated as an observed world condition.
assessments.rationale: The named comparison records incompatible model outputs but has no stipulated basis to privilege one.
assessments.scope: The two declared response rules without an intervention or discriminator.

authorStipulatedConditions.statement: The valve remains closed; models A and B have different declared response rules and no discriminator is stipulated.

claims.proposition: Under the alternative where the valve opens, the synthetic level falls.
claims.scope: The declared alternative and competing models.
claims.temporalQualifier: At the unperformed fixture intervention horizon.

cases.declaredQuestion: What can be said when two declared models disagree about an unperformed alternative?

evidence.description: Model A predicts a fall and model B predicts no change; no intervention occurs.

expressions.form: If the valve had opened, the level would have fallen.
expressions.interpretationNote: The claim belongs to model A's declared alternative world.

cases.lesson: Counterfactual claims are model-relative and not direct observations.
nonClaims: A model output is not direct observation of an alternative world.
The atlas does not rank the competing models.

cases.title: Two counterfactual models without an intervention

assessments.limitations: The atlas does not recommend whether either gate should open and authorizes no action.
assessments.rationale: Congestion is stipulated, but no duty, priority, consent, safety or cost premise connects it to the proposed directive.
assessments.scope: Presence of declared normative bridge premises only.

authorStipulatedConditions.statement: The synthetic north gate is congested; the fixture declares no priority, duty, cost, consent or safety premise.

claims.proposition: The south gate ought to be opened because the north gate is congested.
claims.scope: The invented gate choice and unnamed affected interests.

cases.declaredQuestion: Can a congestion measurement alone establish what ought to be done?

evidence.description: The fixture stipulates congestion but no normative bridge premise.

expressions.form: The north gate is congested, therefore the south gate ought to be opened.
expressions.interpretationNote: The conclusion is normative even though the only declared premise is empirical.

cases.lesson: Normative conclusions require declared normative premises and affected commitments.
nonClaims: An empirical observation does not silently derive an ought.
No gate action is recommended or authorized.
cases.scenario: A synthetic gate is congested. A statement concludes a second gate ought to open without declaring a normative premise.
cases.title: A factual observation that does not supply an ought

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Requires a named comparison or observation and remains revisable.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim whose scoped subject matter is a declared observable condition in the synthetic fixture.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Validity does not establish premise truth or real-world correspondence.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim about formal consequence, compatibility or contradiction under declared premises and rules.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Institutional force does not establish an empirical claim outside its authority.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim about a status created or recognized by a declared synthetic institution under a declared rule.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Conformance and receipt validity do not establish semantic truth.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim about conformance to a declared synthetic procedure, record or protocol.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Multiple scoped interpretations may remain live.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim about meaning, framing, significance or the best reading of declared material.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: A story as a whole is never reduced to one verdict; coherence, fidelity, correspondence, selection and omission remain separate.
claimRegimes.definition: An assessable claim fragment extracted from a separately represented story artifact.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Literal empirical tests may be outside the expression's declared speech act.
claimRegimes.definition: A non-literal comparison offered within a declared language practice.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Fictional status is not deception and does not imply literal-world assertion.
claimRegimes.definition: A proposition inside a declared invented world or fiction practice.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Empirical support alone does not derive the normative conclusion.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim about what ought to be done or valued under declared reasons and commitments.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: The Phase-0 atlas refuses untyped fixed-point adjudication.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim whose interpretation refers to itself or its own assessment status.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Record the report and its conditions without inferring private state, deception or being-wide reliability.
claimRegimes.definition: A first-person report of a declared synthetic subject's apparent experience or perception.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Assess only after the named horizon and preserve the distinction between a reasonable forecast and its eventual outcome.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim about a condition at a declared future fixture time under stated assumptions.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Requires an explicit model or comparison and cannot be collapsed into direct observation.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim about what would occur under a declared alternative synthetic condition.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Assess felicity and authority separately from empirical correspondence and moral legitimacy.
claimRegimes.definition: An utterance that declares, promises, requests, directs or constitutes a scoped institutional relation rather than merely describing one.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Assess the scoped report and access conditions only; never infer witness credibility, worth, identity or a person-wide score.
claimRegimes.definition: A report attributed to a synthetic witness role about that role's declared access to an event or condition.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Temporal order, correlation and narrative sequence do not by themselves establish causation.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim that one declared synthetic condition produced or changed another under an explicit causal model.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Definition fixes scoped use; it neither discovers an empirical condition nor forces identity across languages.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim about stipulated term use within a declared vocabulary or language practice.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Phase 0 may check only the source attribution; support cannot be transferred to the referent proposition.
claimRegimes.definition: A claim that an invented source record advances a stated metaphysical or theological referent proposition.

claimRegimes.assessmentLimit: Phase 0 provides no proof, disproof, equation, ranking or authority over the referent proposition or any tradition.
claimRegimes.definition: The metaphysical or theological referent proposition advanced by an invented source, represented separately from its attribution record.

contradictionRegister.phaseZeroRule: Treat ledger and protocol outputs only as bounded record, integrity or protocol-declared consensus states; never as semantic truth.
contradictionRegister.tension: Older copy describes consensus or validation as moving a claim from asserted to true; the operational bridge says receipts, hashes, agreement and coherence do not establish correspondence or truth.

description: A static synthetic atlas for inspecting typed relations among expression, claim, warrant, reasoning, narrative, provenance, institutional status, assessment and correction without producing a truth oracle.

epistemicSeparations.reason: One expression may admit multiple interpretations and claims.
A representation is not the condition it represents.
Evidence changes warrant under a method; it is not truth as a substance or field.
A valid inference may begin from a false premise.
An internally coherent story may conflict with declared conditions.
Authenticity and integrity do not establish content accuracy.
Agreement and repetition may preserve a shared error.
Authority may constitute a status but cannot decree a physical condition.
Calibrated or emphatic confidence does not itself settle a claim.
Power can shape who is heard independently of access to relevant observations.
Fiction does not present its invented events as literal report.
A correction should remain linked to the record it repairs.
A refusal to disclose is not an assertion of a false proposition.
A receipt can establish narrow record properties only.
Identity disclosure is not a prerequisite for evidential access and anonymity is not a negative witness score.
Assess a scoped report and its access conditions, never a person-wide quality.
A missing record may reflect collection, preservation, access or indexing limits.
Many reports may derive from one upstream assertion.
Translation is a scoped mapping with alternatives and loss, not an inverse identity.
Record lifecycle and correspondence assessment are different dimensions.
A Phase-0 assessment cannot authorize action, enforcement or downstream effects.
Causal assessment requires a declared model and discriminating method.
A vocabulary choice does not make an observed condition obtain.
A first-person report and an external condition require different access and methods.

methodVocabulary.definition: Compare a claim only with explicitly declared synthetic world conditions.
Check whether a conclusion follows under the declared rule and premises.
Check declared origin, signature or transformation continuity without assessing content correspondence.
Inspect whether apparently distinct reports share one declared upstream origin.
Compare selected, omitted and ordered events and attributed causes across narratives.
Compare a speech act or official claim with its declared institutional authority and subject-matter limits.
Check whether a cited item exists in the fixture's declared catalogue without inferring content truth.
Compare a claim's time scope with the fixture's declared update or correction sequence.
Inspect genre, translation, ambiguity, metaphor or fiction before selecting an assessment method.
Compare evidential access with institutional uptake without scoring a witness or source.
Inspect whether a declared causal model and discriminating conditions support more than temporal order or correlation.
Inspect declared normative premises and prevent empirical observations from silently deriving an ought.
Enforce downward-only L0 claim, L1 assessment and L2 audit targeting without a fixed-point verdict.
Compare a scoped prediction only after its named fixture horizon while preserving ex-ante warrant separately.
Compare declared alternative-world models without treating an unobserved counterfactual as direct observation.
Record a first-person phenomenal report and its expression conditions without inferring private state or external correspondence.
Inspect the declared access conditions of one synthetic testimony without producing a witness-wide assessment.
Inspect whether a stipulated definition is used within its declared vocabulary and language practice.
Distinguish the record that an invented source advances a metaphysical or theological referent claim from adjudication of that referent proposition.

predecessorBindings.role: Separates receipts, coherence, provenance, correspondence, intent and authority.
Provides a prior closed receipt vocabulary for disclosed semantic transport and loss.
Provides prior distinctions among word, story, genre, myth, institution and civilisation.
Binds the exact schema accompanying the prior language map.
Provides a prior non-causal influence and aftermath map without determining truth.
Binds the exact schema accompanying the prior reality-influence map.
Preserves the typed distinction among PROVED_IN, SUPPORTED_UNDER_TEST and ASSERTED_BY.
Binds the exact schema accompanying the prior Number, Isness and Theology method atlas.
Binds the human-readable prior method boundary without importing doctrine or theological authority.
Preserves the exact older asserted-to-true consensus metaphor as a contradiction witness.
Preserves the exact older Proof-of-Truth economy summary as a contradiction witness.
Preserves the exact older truth-verification and oracle bridge copy as a contradiction witness.

recordLifecycleStates.definition: The record is the current declared version only at the stated fixture date.
A later record identifies and repairs a declared defect in an earlier record.
A source ceases to advance a record without the atlas inferring why or whether its content was false.
A later record replaces an earlier record for a declared purpose and time.
A source formally removes a prior record from active reliance while historical provenance remains visible.

regimeMethodCompatibility.compatibilityNote: Only declared fixture observations and temporal scopes are admissible.
The method checks consequence under declared rules, not premise correspondence.
Authority and felicity remain scoped to the declared institution.
Procedure, provenance and catalogue existence never establish semantic truth.
Interpretation preserves alternatives, genre, audience and loss.
Only extracted fragments are assessed; the story artifact never receives one disposition.
Literal empirical comparison is unavailable unless separately asserted.
Genre can be checked without treating fiction as deceptive literal report.
Normative premises and affected commitments must be declared separately from empirical facts.
Only structural level safety is assessed; no fixed-point verdict is permitted.
The expression of experience is inspectable; private state and external correspondence are not inferred.
Outcome comparison occurs only at the named horizon and does not back-propagate into intent or competence.
Alternative-world models remain declared models, not direct observations.
Felicity and authority are inspected separately from empirical and moral claims.
Only the report and declared access are assessed, never a witness-wide quality.
A discriminating model is required beyond temporal sequence or correlation.
Definition and translation remain scoped stipulations rather than empirical identity.
The method may establish only that an invented source record advances a referent claim; the referent itself remains outside the Phase-0 method.
The source-attribution method has no compatible supported disposition for the referent proposition itself.
